Power-foam paddle buying guide, Vol. 2: October 2026

In June, the question was which foam paddle hit hardest without costing an organ. In October, the better question is what the damn thing does after you've played with it for a while.

The cheap paddles got much more interesting. Some expensive surfaces aged badly in follow-up testing. Some supposedly durable surfaces disagreed with their own launch reviews. And “tournament approved” still requires you to finish the sentence.

This is Vol. 2, researched through October 11. Vol. 1, from June 4, is still here. Start around $100. Spend more for a specific feel, shape, or better-supported surface life. Your shopping cart does not need a seventh generation of anything.

I rewired a shoe dryer with Gemini and almost got yelled at by physics

Being married to an engineer can be tough sometimes — especially if he sweats through his shoes, soaking wet, every time he plays pickleball. Sometimes through two pairs.

This one started with an SD-68 / FujiHome shoe dryer that sux, and somehow turned into the coolest and fucking craziest thing I've ever done.

This is the saga. Bring a snack.

Saigon humidity is rude. You come back from pickleball or a rainy commute and your shoes are a wet crime scene. So I bought one of those upright shoe dryers — the SD-68 — the kind with nozzles that shove air up into each shoe, a little cabinet, timers, even an ozone button for people who think ozone is a personality.

June 22, 2026 · Build notes

Shrinking YouTube Music to 3 MB

YouTube Music doesn't have an official desktop app. The best community alternative was ytmdesktop — a great project, but it ships about 200 MB of Chromium on disk and holds hundreds of MB of RAM, because that's what Electron apps do. They bundle an entire copy of the Chrome browser inside every app.

I rewrote it with Tauri, which uses your operating system's existing webview instead of bundling a browser. The result — YTM Yagami — is about 3 MB to download.

The tradeoff: on macOS you're running Safari's engine instead of Chrome's, and on Windows you're running Edge's. Most of the time this is invisible. Sometimes — as I'll explain below — it's a small nightmare.

June 22, 2026 · Illustrated guide

The Unhurried Guide to Pickleball

There's a sport.

You hit a plastic ball — a hollow little planet, completely full of holes — with a paddle, over a low net, into a kitchen you are not allowed to cook in. When you hit it right it makes a sound like a tiny door being slammed by a tiny, satisfied man.

That's the whole sport. You basically know it already.

You get two guides. They're foxes. I don't know why they're foxes. I asked them and they just told me they’d always been foxes, and they never thought to change.
